scenes.chapter: Solution 1: write every term with x and y

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's call the first term x, and the second term y.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's call the first term x, and the second term y.

lines.text: The third term is x plus y. The fourth is x plus two y.
lines.caption: The third term is x plus y. The fourth is x plus two y.

lines.text: Keep adding the last two terms, and watch the numbers in front grow.
lines.caption: Keep adding the last two terms, and watch the numbers in front grow.

lines.text: Term ten is twenty-one x plus thirty-four y.
lines.caption: Term ten is twenty-one x plus thirty-four y.

lines.text: Look at the numbers in front. They're the Fibonacci numbers!
lines.caption: Look at the numbers in front. They're the Fibonacci numbers!

lines.text: So our equation is twenty-one x plus thirty-four y equals two thousand twenty-four.
lines.caption: So our equation is twenty-one x plus thirty-four y equals two thousand twenty-four.

lines.text: We want x plus y. So split thirty-four y into twenty-one y plus thirteen y.
lines.caption: We want x plus y. So split thirty-four y into twenty-one y plus thirteen y.

lines.text: Now twenty-one x plus twenty-one y is twenty-one times x plus y.
lines.caption: Now twenty-one x plus twenty-one y is twenty-one times x plus y.

lines.text: Call that sum T, for total. Now twenty-one T plus thirteen y equals two thousand twenty-four.
lines.caption: Call that sum T, for total. Now twenty-one T plus thirteen y equals two thousand twenty-four.

lines.text: To make T big, thirteen y should be as small as possible. So we want a small y.
lines.caption: To make T big, thirteen y should be as small as possible. So we want a small y.

lines.text: y is at least one, so twenty-one T is at most two thousand eleven.

lines.text: Twenty-one times ninety-six is too big, so T is at most ninety-five.
lines.caption: Twenty-one times ninety-six is too big, so T is at most ninety-five.

lines.text: Now let's count down from ninety-five. The leftover must be thirteen times y.
lines.caption: Now let's count down from ninety-five. The leftover must be thirteen times y.

lines.text: T equals ninety-five leaves twenty-nine. That's not a multiple of thirteen.
lines.caption: T equals ninety-five leaves twenty-nine. That's not a multiple of thirteen.

lines.text: Each step down adds twenty-one, so next come fifty, seventy-one, ninety-two, and so on.

lines.text: None of them work, until T equals eighty-four. The leftover is two hundred sixty.

lines.text: Two hundred sixty is thirteen times twenty. So y is twenty!
